redFirst.basis: Regression mode with expectRedFirst false, and the submit carries no test command. The mutation red was watched by hand in a scratch COPY of plugins/ (never in the task tree). First mutation: NO_AUTO_MAINTENANCE dropped from test_hooks._GIT, then `python3 plugins/audit/tests/test_commit_task_work.py --selftest --stage nm-block` exited 1 with ctw-nm1 FAIL naming 'test_hooks._GIT'. Second mutation: maintenance.auto=false dropped from _harness.NO_AUTO_MAINTENANCE, keeping gc.auto=0. That also exited 1: ctw-nm1 listed all six prefixes as missing a setting, and the traced commit recorded a spawned `git maintenance run --auto --quiet --detach`, so gc.auto=0 alone does not stop the spawn. ctw-nm2 stayed PASS under both mutations.

outcome.technical: Hardening, not a fix. The cause of the CI 38792231809 clone ENOENT and of the Windows add -A flake is STILL NOT ESTABLISHED. This change removes one measured background process and nothing more. MEASUREMENT (git 2.53.0, macOS, GIT_TRACE to a file, scratch under tempfile.mkdtemp and removed in finally). In the or-block of test_commit_task_work (15/15 cases), git spawned a DETACHED `git maintenance run --auto` 14 times. None of those runs started gc, repack, pack-objects or prune. Fixture repos held 45/28/28/27 loose objects and 0 packs, against gc.auto 6700 (sampled at more than 27 entries in objects/17) and gc.autoPackLimit 50. So the auto-gc repack hypothesis is refuted. CHANGE: _harness.NO_AUTO_MAINTENANCE = ('-c','maintenance.auto=false','-c','gc.auto=0'), carried by _harness.GIT and by a new _harness.WORKTREE_PAIR_GIT (the worktree_pair builder's former local prefix). It is also carried by test_hooks._GIT, test_integrate_task.GIT, test_run_test_gate._PLAIN_GIT and test_run_test_gate._SM_GIT (now a full prefix, a tuple). The one direct subprocess git call in test_commit_task_work's branch block (the fixture's stash-pop step) now runs through _harness.GIT. NEW STAGE nm-block in test_commit_task_work: ctw-nm1 reads all six prefixes off their modules and asserts both settings on each. It also traces a fixture commit made with _harness.GIT and asserts a commit was traced and no maintenance or gc was spawned. ctw-nm2 is the second-direction control: the same commit without the switch, run with maintenance.autoDetach=false so it leaves nothing in the background, must show a spawn. AFTER, by trace: test_hooks went from 12 maintenance spawns at base (git archive HEAD export) to 0 (232/232 cases). test_integrate_task went from 13 to 0 (30/30 cases). LIMIT: the or-block still spawns 14 times, because 12 come from test__invariants.build's own _git (plain 'git'; that file is outside this task's files) and 2 from the product's commit-task-work commits. The clone that failed in CI also runs through test__invariants._git, so this change does not touch that call's repository. Making it reach there needs test__invariants.py in a task's files. Gates in the task tree: `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py` exit 0 (335/335 files ok, 16449 cases). `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --encoding cp1252` exit 0 (335/335 files ok, both halves ran). `ruff check plugins/audit/tests` exit 0. `vermin -t=3.8- --no-tips --violations plugins/audit/tests` exit 0.
outcome.descriptive: Fixture git prefixes in the declared suites now start no detached background maintenance (measured 12 and 13 spawns down to 0), a pinned case guards them, and the cause of the clone and add flakes stays open.

testsAdded: ctw-nm1 no fixture git call can spawn an auto gc - the shared prefix and every suite's own prefix carry gc.auto=0 - measured with GIT_TRACE on a heavy fixture (and maintenance.auto=false beside it: every fixture git prefix carries both settings, and a fixture commit traced with the shared prefix spawns no background maintenance)
ctw-nm2 SECOND-DIRECTION CASE: the same traced commit WITHOUT the switch does spawn maintenance
